assumptions: The inert subtree covers the whole hero chrome. The h1, subtitle and talk button were already wrapped by the existing INERT spread, and I extended the same spread to Play.

Browser verification used a production build (next build / next start on port 3102). The dev server kept full-reloading from game-dev's in-progress edits, which remounted the hero before the intro could be observed.
The page CSP has media-src 'self' blob:, so the test video was served same-origin through a playwright route to /intro-test.mp4. No file was added to the repo.

The worktree's node_modules was a dangling symlink to a removed worktree. I replaced it with a real npm ci install (gitignored). The portfolio2 node_modules could not be used because it lacks @react-three/rapier.
questions: components/game/__tests__/tween.test.ts (game-dev's uncommitted change) fails the 'first visible step within 1.25x the median step' test. Should game-dev fix it before npm test can exit 0?
decisionsProposed: IntroVideo reports its cover state through an onActiveChange callback, and TalkingAvatar owns inert and prefetch gating from it (replaces the DOM querySelector check). Active covers the playing and fading phases, so controls stay inert until the cover is removed.
lessonsProposed: Testing Library role queries and accessible names ignore aria-hidden or inert subtrees, so an inert-state test must query by text.
Dev-server browser checks are unreliable while another specialist edits the same worktree (Fast Refresh remounts). Use a production build for evidence.
NEXT_PUBLIC_INTRO_VIDEO_URL must be same-origin because of the CSP media-src.
